longPress.question: What do you want to do with this suggestion?
longPress.whyDefault: This suggestion is based on patterns detected in your expenses this month. The CTA action is the most direct lever to move the number.
longPress.blockSuccessBody: You won't see more "{{family}}" signals until you unblock them from Settings.
longPress.blockErrorBody: Try again in a few seconds.

empty.firstTimeBody: Add your income and a couple of expenses so the assistant can look at your numbers.
empty.reviewedBody: The assistant keeps watching your numbers. If the patterns persist, the suggestions will come back.

dispatcher.saveAnswerErrorBody: Try again in a few seconds.
dispatcher.cancelIntentErrorBody: Try again in a few seconds.

planner.label: Planner
planner.description: I show you the numbers and the details: you like to understand before acting.

firefighter.label: Reactive
firefighter.description: I only ping you when something matters; the rest of the time, I leave you alone.

avoider.label: Cautious
avoider.description: I speak calmly and step by step, with small moves you can actually make.

optimizer.label: Optimizer
optimizer.description: I look for chances to save and make the most of the good months.

copy.recoveryHard_loss: If you don't drop to {{newCupo}} a day, the month is going to close {{overspend}} more expensive than you planned, and that complicates next month too.
copy.recoveryHard_gain: By spending less than {{newCupo}} a day over these {{diasRestantes}} days, you'll reach month-end without going over.
copy.recoveryHard_neutral: To finish the month well you'd have to spend less than {{newCupo}} a day — that's very little. Better to lower your savings target a bit, or push a big payment to later.
copy.velocitySlowerOver: Even though you're going easier than usual, you're still {{over}} above what you planned. Keep it up and you'll make it.
copy.velocitySlower: You're spending more calmly than usual — that's how you reach month-end fine.
copy.velocityFaster_loss_over: If you keep spending like this, the month is going to close {{over}} more expensive than you planned. Ease off a bit these days and you'll make it.
copy.velocityFaster_loss: You're a little fast for this point in the month, but you can still make it. Watch the next few days.
copy.velocityFaster_gain_over: By spending {{over}} less over the rest of the month, you'll land right on what you planned.
copy.velocityFaster_gain: You're doing well, within what you planned for this month.
copy.velocityFaster_neutral_over: At this pace, the month is going to close {{over}} more expensive than you planned. Ease off a bit and you'll make it.
copy.velocityFaster_neutral: If you keep this up, you'll reach month-end without going over what you planned.
copy.fijosRatio_loss: Your fixed expenses (rent, utilities, subscriptions) eat up a big chunk of your salary: if an unexpected expense shows up, you've got almost no cushion left. Lowering the biggest one frees up {{excess}} a month.
copy.fijosRatio_gain: If you lower your fixed expenses (rent, utilities, subscriptions), you keep {{excess}} more a month for daily life or for saving. The biggest one moves the needle most.
copy.fijosRatio_neutral: Your fixed expenses (rent, utilities, subscriptions) take up a big chunk of your salary: little is left to eat, go out and save. Lowering the biggest one frees up {{excess}} a month.
copy.positiveForecastGoal_loss: If you don't save it now, that leftover ({{sobra}}) will go into next month's expenses. Move {{proposed}} to "{{goalTitle}}" before it's gone.
copy.positiveForecastGoal_gain: You're ahead: at month-end you've got {{sobra}} to spare. Take advantage and move {{proposed}} to "{{goalTitle}}".
copy.positiveForecastGoal_neutral: If you keep this up, at month-end you've got {{sobra}} to spare. A good move: send {{proposed}} to "{{goalTitle}}" and keep the rest saved just in case.
copy.positiveForecast_loss: You'll have {{sobra}} to spare at month-end — easy to spend without noticing. Better decide now where to keep it.
copy.positiveForecast_gain: Good month: you've got {{sobra}} to spare. Great time to start a savings goal.
copy.positiveForecast_neutral: If you keep this up, at month-end you've got {{sobra}} to spare. That money can go to a savings goal or stay put just in case.
copy.fijosRatio_dynamic: Your fixed payments (rent, utilities, subscriptions) take a very large share of what came in this cycle: if an income runs late, there's almost no cushion left. Lowering the biggest one frees up {{excess}} per cycle.

superStorm.title: Critical confluence
superStorm.body_two: Two factors are lining up: {{factors}}. A full plan is suggested.
superStorm.body_three: Three factors are lining up: {{factors}}. A full plan is suggested.
superStorm.explanation: When fixed expenses weigh too much and at the same time you're spending more than you have available today or you sped up spending in the last few days, it's not an isolated problem: it's the sum. The full plan lowers both the structural pressure and the day-to-day at once.

superSavings.title: Positive streak
superSavings.body: You've got a sustained streak, the month closes with money to spare, and there are categories in your favor. Now's the time to take advantage: raise the goal or reassign the leftover.
superSavings.explanation: The combination of three positive signals at once — streak, leftover money and a category win — sustains real change. Good moment to raise the goal or put the leftover to work.

stressWeek.title: {{count}} fixed expenses due in 7 days
stressWeek.body: {{names}} add up to {{total}}. It's better to set that amount aside to avoid surprises.
stressWeek.bodyMore_one: {{names}} and {{count}} more add up to {{total}}. It's better to set that amount aside to avoid surprises.
stressWeek.bodyMore_other: {{names}} and {{count}} more add up to {{total}}. It's better to set that amount aside to avoid surprises.
stressWeek.explanation: A "fixed expense" is a recurring monthly payment (rent, utilities, subscriptions). When several land in the same week, fewer pesos are left for day-to-day spending. We warn you ahead of time to avoid surprises.

paydayProximity.title: You have {{remaining}} left and {{days}} days until payday
paydayProximity.body: To reach the next payday in good shape, spend up to {{perDay}} a day.
paydayProximity.explanation: It's what you have left divided by the days until your next payday: how much you can spend per day without hitting zero.

endAcceleration.title: You're spending {{perDay}}/day, above your average
endAcceleration.body: These last 3 days you spent {{last3Avg}}/day against {{cycleAvg}}/day for the rest of the month. {{days}} days left — at this pace, the month ends in the red.
endAcceleration.explanation: It's common to loosen control at the end of the month, right when spending spikes most. Comparing the last 3 days against the month's average helps catch the change in time.

recoveryHard.title: You overspent quite a bit today
recoveryHard.explanation: When you spend much more than you have available today, cutting how much you can spend for the rest of the month doesn't work. Better to readjust the savings goal or reorder a fixed expense than to hold an impossible target.

recoverySoft.title: I adjusted how much you can spend per day
recoverySoft.body: You overspent by {{overspend}} today. If you spend {{newCupo}}/day from now to month-end, the month still closes fine.
recoverySoft.explanation: When the excess is moderate, it spreads across the remaining days and leaves a slightly lower daily limit. If you stick to that limit, the month closes within budget.

velocity.explanation: It compares your recent spending pace (last 7 days) against the month's average. If spending sped up, it estimates the closing amount to anticipate how the month will end.

positiveForecast.title: Money to spare: {{sobra}}
positiveForecast.explanation: It estimates the month's close by combining your current spending pace with the days remaining. When the result is positive, it shows how much money you have to spare for your savings goal or reserve.

catAccel.bodySpike: You spent {{amount}} on {{category}} this month, against {{avg}} usually. Almost all of it was this past week — maybe something one-off (a trip, a gift, a big purchase). Was it that or did something change?
catAccel.bodyTrend: You spent {{amount}} on {{category}} this month, against {{avg}} usually. It's been creeping up. Do you want to rein it in or is it now part of your expenses?
catAccel.title: {{category}} jumped this month{{suffix}}
catAccel.explanation: It compares what you're spending now in a category with what you usually spend. Seeing it in time lets you decide whether to rein it in or if it's a one-off.
catAccel.fuseShare: On top of that, it already takes up {{pct}}% of everything you spent this month: that's where you can save the most.

cap.bodyBreach: Your limit was {{cap}} and you've spent {{spent}}. Over by {{excess}}.
cap.bodyWarning: You've spent {{spent}} of the {{cap}} you set as a limit. {{remaining}} left to close the month.
cap.explanation: If you set a monthly cap on a category, the app warns you when you get close or go over it. It works like a personal goal: it helps rein in spending before it affects the month's close.

catDominance.title: {{category}} takes {{amount}} of your spending
catDominance.body: Of the {{total}} you spent this month, {{amount}} went to {{category}}. Spending a little less there shows up more than trimming several small categories.
catDominance.explanation: When one category concentrates nearly half the spending, that's where you can save most. A small cut in that category frees up more money than several small tweaks elsewhere.

catWin.title: {{category}} −{{pct}}% vs average
catWin.body: You spent {{now}} this month vs {{avg}} on average. If you keep it up, that's {{annual}} a year.
catWin.explanation: It spots categories where this month's spending is clearly below the historical average. Showing the yearly equivalent helps sustain the change over time.

smallLeaks.title: {{count}} small expenses add up to {{total}}
smallLeaks.body: Purchases under $5,000 (kiosk, delivery, coffee) make up {{pct}}% of the month's spending. They tend to go unnoticed one by one.
smallLeaks.explanation: Expenses under $5,000 seem trivial one by one, but together they add up to a big slice of the month. Seeing them together helps spot where the budget "drip" concentrates.

nightImpulse.title: {{amount}} on late-night purchases
nightImpulse.body: {{count}} of {{total}} purchases were made after 10pm, adding up to {{amount}}. At night, relaxed at home, it's easier to overspend without thinking.
nightImpulse.explanation: Buying at night, relaxed at home, tends to lead to overspending. Leaving the purchase for the next day helps cut several of those.

weeklyPattern.bodyDow: On {{day}} you spend quite a bit more than a normal day. Across the month, that adds up to {{extra}} extra.
weeklyPattern.explanationDow: It groups spending by day of the week and computes the average for each. It pinpoints the day that concentrates the most recurring spending.
weeklyPattern.bodyWeekend: Monday to Friday you spend {{weekday}} a day. Saturdays and Sundays, {{weekend}} a day. That's where you can cut the most.
weeklyPattern.explanationWeekend: Weekends concentrate outings, delivery and social plans that raise the spending average. Small tweaks on Saturday and Sunday add up to several thousand at close without affecting the rest of the week.

fijosRatio.title: Your fixed expenses weigh too much
fijosRatio.explanation: When your fixed expenses pass half your salary, very little is left for unexpected costs and savings.
fijosRatio.explanationDynamic: Compares your fixed payments against the income you logged this cycle. When they pass half, little margin is left for day-to-day.

incomeVolatility.titleBetter: You earned {{amount}} this month — more than usual
incomeVolatility.titleWorse: You earned {{amount}} this month — less than usual
incomeVolatility.bodyBetter: Other months you earned around {{avg}}; this month {{delta}} more came in. Good time to save a bit of that difference.
incomeVolatility.bodyWorse: Other months you earned around {{avg}}; this month {{delta}} less came in. Watch your spending until it recovers.
incomeVolatility.explanation: It compares what you earned this month with what you usually earn. If quite a bit less comes in, it's worth watching spending; if more comes in, save the difference.

subUsage.titleHard: You haven't been using {{name}} for ~2 months
subUsage.bodyHard: You said you barely use {{name}} and it costs {{amount}}/mo. Do you really need to pay for it? Cancelling it saves you {{annual}} a year.
subUsage.titleSoft: {{name}}: are you getting value from it?
subUsage.bodySoft: The last few times you said you use it little. It costs {{amount}}/mo — if you're not getting value, it's worth reviewing.
subUsage.titlePay: You paid {{name}} · how much did you use it?
subUsage.bodyPay: We logged the payment for {{name}} ({{amount}}/mo). How much did you use it last month?
subUsage.bodyReask: It's been a while since you told us how {{name}} ({{amount}}/mo) is going. Are you still using it?
subUsage.explanation: We ask about the subscriptions you pay for to see if you actually use them. If you keep saying no, we let you know so you can decide whether they're worth paying for.

hike.title: {{name}}: {{pct}}% increase
hike.body: It went from {{prev}} to {{next}}. Over 12 months that's {{annual}} more. Comparing other providers or renegotiating can recover part of the increase.
hike.explanation: It detects increases in fixed expenses as they're added. The increases seem small month to month, but built up over a year they often justify looking for alternatives or renegotiating with the provider.

savingsFeasibility.title: For "{{goal}}" you're short {{shortfall}} this month
savingsFeasibility.body: To get there on time you'd have to save about {{perWeek}} a week. This month you're at {{actual}} — save a little more and you'll make it.
savingsFeasibility.explanation: It compares what you're saving this month with what you need to reach your goal on time. Adjusting early makes the effort smaller.

savingsOver.body: This month you saved {{actual}} when the plan asked for {{planned}}. At this pace, {{goal}} arrives in {{newMonths}} months instead of {{months}}.
savingsOver.explanation: When monthly savings beat the plan, we recompute the estimated completion date. You can keep the pace to arrive sooner or raise the goal.

highSingle.title: Big charge today: {{price}}
highSingle.body: Today you logged {{price}} in a single charge — {{pct}}% of what you can spend today ({{cupo}}). See if it's worth balancing out the rest of the day.
highSingle.explanation: When a single expense takes a big share of what you can spend today, the rest of the day is very committed. Seeing it right away lets you react.

duplicate.title: {{count}} similar charges in 48h
duplicate.body: I spotted {{count}} charges for "{{description}}" at ~{{amount}} in under 48h. Can you confirm they're different?
duplicate.explanation: Two charges with almost identical description and amount within a few hours are usually a duplicate from the merchant or the manual entry. The idea is for the user to confirm it.

dataGap.body: If you had movements those days, log them so the month's close reflects reality. If not, ignore this notice.
dataGap.explanation: Signals depend on expenses being logged. A long pause without records usually means something wasn't recorded, not that nothing was spent.

savingsMilestone.title: You hit the goal!
savingsMilestone.body: You completed 100% of "{{goal}}" with {{amount}} saved. Good time to set the next one.
savingsMilestone.explanation: A milestone is for celebrating and riding the momentum: the next goal starts with the habit already built, not from scratch.

incomeMissing.title: Expected income not confirmed
incomeMissing.body: Your income was expected but the cycle wasn't confirmed. If it arrived, update the new cycle's balance. If the date changed, adjust your payday.
incomeMissing.explanation: When your configured payday has passed but the month wasn't confirmed, the rest of the math (what you can spend today) works off the previous month. Confirming here resets the baseline.

cycleStart.title: Tight month: {{pct}}% free
cycleStart.bodyWithGoal: After fixed expenses and the goal, you've got {{libre}} free ({{pct}}% of income). When it's low, any surprise leaves you short. Pausing the goal this month or renegotiating a fixed expense gives you breathing room.
cycleStart.bodyNoGoal: After fixed expenses, you've got {{libre}} free ({{pct}}% of income). When it's low, any surprise leaves you short. Pausing the goal this month or renegotiating a fixed expense gives you breathing room.
cycleStart.explanation: "Free" is what's left of your income after paying fixed expenses and setting aside the savings goal. If it starts low, any surprise leaves you short. Better to flag it at the start of the month while there's still time to adjust.

forecastPaydayGap.body_one: If you spend like the last few days, you'll hit $0 about {{count}} day before your next payday. There's time to fix it if you cut back now.
forecastPaydayGap.body_other: If you spend like the last few days, you'll hit $0 about {{count}} days before your next payday. There's time to fix it if you cut back now.
forecastPaydayGap.explanation: We compare what you have left with what you could end up spending in the worst case (expensive days + fixed expenses). If the math comes out less than the days left until payday, this alert lights up.

streak.title: {{count}} days in a row without going over
streak.body: You're in control. At this pace, the month's close leaves {{amount}} unspent.
streak.explanation: It counts days in a row where the day's spending stayed under control. Seeing the streak reinforces the habit and makes the month's progress visible.

incomeMissingDynamic.title: No income logged this cycle yet
incomeMissingDynamic.body: A good part of the cycle has passed and no income is logged. If money already came in, log it so your daily allowance reflects what you really have.
incomeMissingDynamic.explanation: In variable income mode, your budget builds from the income you log. With no income logged, the daily allowance works with $0.

followup.titleAwaiting_one: {{count}} day ago you were going to cancel {{name}}.
followup.titleAwaiting_other: {{count}} days ago you were going to cancel {{name}}.
followup.askNoPayment: Can you confirm you cancelled it?

classification.consensusBody_other:

salaryPending.detail: Confirm your latest payday and I'll bring this month's numbers up to date.

overToday.detail: You spent more than you had for today, and there's {{remaining}} until your next payday.

overdue.detail_one: You have {{count}} overdue fixed expense and {{amount}} still unpaid.
overdue.detail_other: You have {{count}} overdue fixed expenses and {{amount}} still unpaid.

adjustDaily.title: A small tweak gets you there
adjustDaily.detail: Spending about {{amount}} less per day gets you comfortably to month-end.

dueSoon.detail_one: {{count}} fixed expense is coming up, so it's worth setting aside {{amount}} to avoid running short by month-end.
dueSoon.detail_other: {{count}} fixed expenses are coming up, so it's worth setting aside {{amount}} to avoid running short by month-end.

zeroStreak.detail: You've gone {{count}} days in a row without spending — that leaves you more money for the rest of the month.

steady.title: The cycle is under control
steady.detail: There's {{remaining}} until payday and you're still within the expected range today.

noBase.title: Finish your financial setup first
noBase.detail: Without income, a savings goal and a payday, there's no reliable reference to make decisions.

salaryPending.title: Confirm your payday before logging more
salaryPending.detail: Doing it now keeps the new cycle from getting mixed up with the previous one.

overToday.title: Today it's best to cut variable spending
overToday.detail: If you stop here, tomorrow you'll open with {{opening}}.

remainingToday.title: Use what's still left for today as your guide
remainingToday.detail: Your real cap for the rest of the day is {{remaining}}.

overdue.title: Pay your overdue fixed expenses first
overdue.detail_one: There's {{count}} overdue item and it's already pushing the cycle.
overdue.detail_other: There are {{count}} overdue items and they're already pushing the cycle.

reserve.title: Set money aside for the fixed expenses coming up
reserve.detail: Setting aside {{amount}} keeps you from running short when your next fixed expenses are due.

flexibleOver.title: You've already gone over your day-to-day budget
flexibleOver.detail: Your plan (half for fixed expenses, {{flexiblePct}}% for day-to-day and {{savingsPct}}% for savings) left you {{target}} for day-to-day, and you've already spent {{spent}}.

adjustDaily.title: It's worth spending a bit less per day
adjustDaily.detail: From tomorrow, try to cut about {{amount}} per day.

zeroStreak.title: Protect the money you've already saved
zeroStreak.detail_one: You've already gone {{count}} day in a row without spending.
zeroStreak.detail_other: You've already gone {{count}} days in a row without spending.

onPlan.title: You're on track with your monthly plan
onPlan.detail: You still have {{remaining}} for day-to-day spending this month.

protectSavings.title: Avoid dipping into savings if you don't have to
protectSavings.detail: There's still {{remaining}} of your savings goal untouched.

noBase.title: Turn on your control framework first
noBase.detail: A clear financial baseline is what turns your history into useful decisions.

adjustDaily.title: Fix your daily pace before reworking the whole budget
adjustDaily.detail: The suggested adjustment is {{amount}} per day for the rest of the month.

dailyCap.title: Use a daily cap instead of reviewing each expense in isolation
dailyCap.detail: The simple cap to hold the close is {{amount}} per day.

topCategory.title: Start with {{category}}
topCategory.detail: {{category}} already accounts for {{pct}}% of the month.

recurringFocus.title: Audit repeat spending before the small stuff
recurringFocus.detail: "{{label}}" showed up {{count}} times and adds up to {{total}}.

committed.title: Set aside what's committed first, then look at the rest
committed.detail: There's {{amount}} committed across fixed expenses, installments and debt this month.

weekend.title: Set a specific limit for the weekend
weekend.detail: Weekends run {{pct}}% above your Monday-to-Friday average.

steady.title: Keep your current pace and keep logging
steady.detail: You still have {{remaining}} today and the projection isn't flagging anything serious.
